I attacked the verifier's own correction first, because the place a verifier is likeliest to introduce a fresh error is the word it changed, and because the reading I carried in my head was the unprovable. The correction holds and my memory was wrong.

WHAT I DID. I fetched the electronic text the verifier names (sackett.net) myself and extracted it independently with pdftotext, rather than trusting the extraction already sitting in this session's scratch directory. Both extractions agree, and what comes out is clean retyped prose, not OCR mush: “The unknown,” said Faxe's soft voice in the forest, “the unforetold, the unproven, that is what life is based on. Ignorance is the ground of thought. Unproof is the ground of action. If it were proven that there is no God there would be no religion.” Word for word what the verifier proposes, once the dialogue tag is lifted out.

SECOND WITNESS, because one unofficial ebook is thin. Wikiquote's Le Guin page does not carry the passage at all: I pulled the raw wikitext, 120 KB of it, and searched it, and there is no hit on unforetold, so Wikiquote neither helps nor hurts. A phrase search does decide it. The phrase the unforetold, the unproven returns quotation entries printing the sentence in exactly this wording, including one that prints the whole dialogue tag as the book has it. The phrase the unforetold, the unprovable returns nothing whatever. The reading I suspected does not exist in circulation, let alone in a text. Two witnesses to unproven, none to unprovable, and the pairing with the next sentence, if it were proven that there is no God, is what a copy editor would expect.

LOCATOR. The chapter heads in the text run 4. The Nineteenth Day, 5. The Domestication of Hunch, 6. One Way into Orgoreyn, and the passage sits a dozen lines above the chapter 6 head, at the close of chapter 5, during the walk with Faxe under the dark branches of the Forest of Otherhord. Chapter and chapter title are right, and so is the parenthetical Otherhord in the evidence.

SPEAKER. It is Faxe's line, not Genly Ai's, and the source names Faxe in parentheses after the locator, which is what rule 5 and the two speaker traps in the misattribution list ask for. The note discloses that the interpolated tag has been removed, which is the honest way to print it, and no word has been invented to bridge the gap: the sentence reads continuously in the book.

OTHER GATES. shipped.js: shipped empty, near empty, ursula k. le guin at 0 of 3, not banned. The line is on no trap in the misattribution list. Scope: a novel of 1969, not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory, and well before 1999. Publishable: nothing here needs a warning. Tag Fiction is the form of the work. Source line is 93 characters, leads with the author's name, carries no dash and no straight quote, and runs work, then locator, then speaker, then year. Theme fit is real rather than ornamental: unproof is the ground of action is a line about moving before you are sure, which is the July theme at six in the morning, though it reaches it through epistemology rather than through heroics.

THE ONE WEAKNESS I WOULD LEAVE ON THE RECORD. No print edition was opened, and the evidence block says so plainly, which is the right way to file it. The source line names no edition, only the year, so nothing false reaches the card; rule 4 is met by the chapter and chapter title. If the owner ever wants belt and braces on this one, the fix is a page in a named setting, not a change of wording.
